caption:
A decade ago, almost no property buyer in India was from abroad. Now nearly one in five is.

NRI buyers now make up nearly 20% of Indian property purchases, up from around 7% in 2015 - nearly tripling in just ten years. Bengaluru and Mumbai are the top two destinations, together accounting for over half of all NRI buyer preference.

This is happening alongside record remittances - $135 billion sent home last year, up 14% from the year before, giving the diaspora more capital to invest.

This isn't diaspora money passing through India. It's diaspora money staying in India, as property, for decades. A house isn't a quick transaction - it's a twenty-year bet on the place you buy it in, made by people who could have put that money anywhere else in the world.

Sources: Business Today, Ghar.tv, Business Standard (2025-2026)
